indications:
Clobetasol Propionate is indicated for adults, elderly and children over 1 year in following dermatoses.
• Psoriasis (excluding widespread plaque psoriasis)
• Recalcitrant dermatoses
• Lichen planus
• Discoid lupus erythematosus
• Other skin conditions which do not respond satisfactorily½ to less potent steroids
dosage_and_administration: Adults, elderly and children over 1 year: Apply a thin layer of Clobetasol Propionate Cream or Ointment½ to the affected skin areas twice daily and rub in gently and completely. Repeated short courses of Clobetasol Propionate may be used½ to control exacerbations. In more resistant lesions, especially where there is hyperkeratosis, the effect of Clobetasol can be enhanced, if necessary, by occluding the treatment area with polythene film. Overnight occlusion only is usually adequate½ to bring about a satisfactory response. Clobetasol Propionate is super-high potency½ topical corticosteroids; therefore, treatment should be limited½ to 2 consecutive weeks. The maximum weekly dose should not be exceeded 50 gm/week. In case of children, courses should be limited if possible½ to five days and reviewed weekly.
administration_route: Route of administration: Cutaneous. Creams are especially appropriate for moist or weeping surfaces. Ointments are especially appropriate for dry, lichenified or scaly lesions.
contraindications: It is contraindicated in patient with hypersensitivity½ to any component of the preparation. It should not be used in rosacea, acne vulgaris, perioral dermatitis, perianal and genital pruritus, pruritus without inflammation, untreated cutaneous infections.
side_effects: The most reported side effects are burning and stinging sensation. Less frequent adverse reactions are itching, skin atrophy, cracking and fissuring of the skin. Cushing syndrome has been reported in infants and adults as a result of prolonged use of½ topical Clobetasol Propionate formulations.
precautions_and_warnings: In case of using occlusive dressings, the skin should be cleansed before a fresh dressing is applied. Topical corticosteroids should be used with caution in psoriasis as rebound relapses, and development of local or systemic½ toxicity due½ to impaired barrier function of the skin may occur. If used on the face, treatment should be limited½ to 5 days. When Clobetasol Propionate used on eyelids, care should be taken½ to avoid the eyes as cataract and glaucoma might result from repeated exposure.
pregnancy_and_lactation:
There are limited data from the use of Clobetasol Propionate cream in pregnant women. Topical administration of corticosteroids½ to pregnant animals can cause abnormalities of foetal development. The relevance of this finding½ to humans has not been established. However, the administration of Clobetasol Propionate Cream during pregnancy and lactation should only be considered if the expected benefit½ to the mother outweighs the possible risks of treatment.
It is unknown whether this drug is excreted in human milk. Because many drugs are excreted in human milk, caution should be exercised when Clobetasol Propionate Cream is administered½ to a nursing woman.
drug_interactions: Co-administered drugs that can inhibit CYP3A4 (eg ritonavir, itraconazole) have been shown½ to inhibit the metabolism of corticosteroids leading½ to increased systemic exposure.
pharmacology: Clobetasol Propionate is a very potent½ topical corticosteroid. It has anti-inflammatory, antipruritic and vasoconstrictive properties. It shows anti-inflammatory activity via multiple mechanisms½ to inhibit late phase allergic reactions. It decreases the density of mast cells, chemotaxis and activation of eosinophils. It also reduces cytokine production and inhibits the metabolism of arachidonic acid.
pediatric_usage: In infants and children under 12 years of age, long-term continuous½ topical corticosteroid therapy should be avoided where possible, as adrenal suppression can occur. Children are more susceptible½ to the use of½ topical corticosteroids which develops atrophic changes.
overdose_effects: Acute overdosage is very unlikely½ to occur, however, in the case of chronic over-dosage or misuse the features of hypercortisolism may occur and in this situation½ topical steroid should be discontinued.
storage_conditions: Keep below 30°C temperature, protected from light and moisture. Do not freeze. Keep out of the reach of children.

The usual adult dosage is 1 gram administered intravenously or intramuscularly every 8½ to 12 hours. The dosage and route should be determined by the susceptibility of the causative organisms, the severity of infection and the condition, and renal function of the patient.
Ceftazidime is½ to be used by the parenteral route, the dosage depending upon the severity, sensitivity & type of infections and the age, weight & renal function of the patient.
Adults: The adult dosage range for ceftazidime is 1½ to 6 gm per day 8 or 12 hourly (IM/IV) in the majority of infections, 1 gm 8 hourly or 2 gm 12 hourly should be given.
• In urinary tract infections and many less serious infections: 500 mg or 1 gm 12 hourly is usually adequate.
• In severe infections, especially immunocompromised patients, including those with neutropenia: 2 gm 8 or 12 hourly should be administered. When used as a prophylactic agent in prostatic surgery 1 gm should be given at the induction of anesthesia. A second dose should be considered at the time of catheter removal.
Elderly: In view of the reduced clearance of Ceftazidime in acutely ill elderly patients, the daily dosage should not normally exceed 3 gm, especially in those over 80 years of age.
• Cystic fibrosis: In fibrocystic adults with normal renal function who have pseudomonal lung infections, high doses of 100½ to 150 mg/kg/day as three divided doses should be used.

Angioedema and anaphylaxis have been reported very rarely. Gastrointestinal symptoms are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. precautions_and_warnings: The½ total daily dosage should be reduced when Ceftazidime is administered½ to patients with renal insufficiency. Ceftazidime should be prescribed with caution in individuals with a history of gastrointestinal disease, particularly colitis.
pregnancy_and_lactation:

A wide range of gram-negative organisms is susceptible½ to ceftazidime in vitro, including strains resistant½ to gentamicin and other aminoglycosides. It is highly stable½ to most clinically important beta-lactamases, plasmid or chromosomal, which are produced by both gram-negative and gram-positive organisms and, consequently, is active against many strains resistant½ to ampicillin and other cephalosporins.

overdose_effects: Ceftazidime overdosage has occurred in patients with renal failure. Reactions have included seizure activity, encephalopathy, asterixis, neuromuscular excitability, and coma. Patients who receive an acute overdosage should be carefully observed and given supportive treatment.
storage_conditions: Store below 25°C, protected from light and moisture. Reconstituted solutions are stable for up½ to 24 h if stored between 2°-8°C.

Read moreZinc Sulfate Monohydrate is indicated in zinc deficiency and/or zinc losing conditions. Zinc deficiency can occur as a result of inadequate diet or malabsorption. Excessive loss of zinc can occur in trauma, burns, diarrhoea and protein losing conditions. A zinc supplement is given until clinical improvement occurs but it may need½ to be continued in severe malabsorption, metabolic disease or in zinc losing states.
dosage_and_administration:
Child under 10 kg: 5 ml (1 teaspoonful) 2 times daily after food.
Child between 10-30 kg: 10 ml (2 teaspoonfuls) 1-3 times daily after food.
Adults and child over 30 kg: 20 ml (4 teaspoonfuls) 1-3 times daily after food.
This drug is most effective if they are taken at least 1 hour before or 2 hour after meals. However, if causes stomach upset, this may be taken with a meal.
administration_route:
For dispersible tablet-
• Place the tablet in a teaspoon
• Add adequate amount of water
• Let the tablet dissolve completely
• Give the entire spoonful solution
contraindications: It is contraindicated in those who are hypersensitive½ to any component of the ingredient of this preparation.
side_effects: Zinc may cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach upset, heartburn and gastritis.
precautions_and_warnings: In acute renal failure, zinc accumulation may occur in body; so dose adjustment is needed.
pregnancy_and_lactation: The safety of this product in human pregnancy has not been established. Zinc crosses the placenta and is present in breast milk.
drug_interactions: Concomitant intake of a tetracycline and zinc may decrease the absorption of both the tetracycline and zinc. Similarly concomitant administration of zinc and quinolone drug may also decrease the absorption of both. Concomitant intake of penicillamine and zinc may decrese absorption of zinc.
pharmacology: Zinc sulphate monohydrate is an essential trace element and is involved in a number of body enzyme systems. The body needs zinc for normal growth and health. Zinc is also vital for sexual maturation and reproduction, dark vision adaptation, olfactory and gustatory activity, insulin storage & release and for a variety of host immune defenses. Zinc deficiency may lead½ to impaired immune function, delayed wound healing, a decrease in sense of taste and smell, a reduced ability½ to fight infections, poor night vision, increased risk of abortion, alopecia, mental lethargy, skin changes and poor development of reproductive organs.
storage_conditions: Keep in a dry place away from light and heat. Keep out of the reach of children.
